LESSON: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING PROJECT

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: COMMUNITY SERVICE-LEARNING
Topic 2.1: Community Service Learning Project
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Community Service Learning Project, part of COMMUNITY SERVICE-LEARNING in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: What does one consider while implementing a project? 2. Why is reflection important in a project?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Community Service Learning Project together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: learners discuss, brainstorm, and consult on various project/activity processes.

• Self-efficacy: learners develop the skills of self-awareness and leadership as they undertake the CSL project.

• Creativity and Imagination: learners come up with creative ways of solving the identified problem in the community

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners identify a community need or gaps and explore plausible solutions to address

the gaps.

• Digital Literacy: learners use technology as they search for solutions to the identified problem in the community.

• Learning to Learn: learners gain new knowledge and skills as they discuss and work together to address a community

problem in the project.

• Citizenship: learners participate in CSL projects to address community challenges thereby enhancing their sense of civic

consciousness and belonging.

9

Values:
• Social Justice: learners carry out research using digital devices and print media and also use resources in the process of

planning to address the community problem.

• Unity: learners engage, discuss, search, and plan for the project in the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Governance: learners work with community members and the local leadership in providing solutions to the identified issues

in society.

• Critical thinking Skills: learners brainstorm possible solutions to the identified problem in the community.
